why: The tracks lead to Mapleton and Brown asks 'Should I change it first or not?' about what 'shall be there', so a reader can fairly ask whether the horse's appearance is to be altered.

text: Were the horse's looks changed? — yes
why: Brown's own words 'change it first' give the reader reason to consider a change of looks; the label is an open possibility, not a revealed fact.

text: Were the horse's looks changed? — no
why: Brown's 'or not' leaves it open, so 'no change' is the natural alternative possibility.
